output.subject: We've received your complaint about app access, overdraft fees and calls
output.body:
Dear ⟦CUSTOMER_NAME_1⟧,

Thank you for writing to us. We have received your complaint, and we have read it carefully.

You told us that you have been locked out of the app since September 8, with a message saying your device can't be verified. You mentioned that because you couldn't move money from savings, two automatic payments overdrew your checking account and you were charged two $34 overdraft fees. You also told us that you called twice to sort this out, and both times you waited on hold for over an hour before the call dropped.

You've asked for the fees to be refunded, for your app access to be fixed, and for an apology. We have noted each of these requests.

We're sorry for the frustration and inconvenience this has caused, especially given what you described about trying to reach us by phone. A specialist team is reviewing your complaint, and we will respond within 10 business days.

Thank you for your patience while we look into this.

Customer Care, Meridian Harbor Bank
notes_for_analyst: Check whether the app lockout is still active and whether the customer needs help regaining access before the full response.
Check for further automatic payments that could cause more overdrafts while the customer is locked out.
Decide on the request to refund the two $34 overdraft fees.
Decide whether a formal apology is appropriate once the facts are reviewed.
Review call records for the two calls the customer says dropped after more than an hour on hold.
Confirm the lockout start date of September 8 and the dates of the two overdraft fees.
The reply takes no position on the issues; the specialist team owns the substantive response.
